cover.headline: A pain-and-rheumatology franchise with its own APIs, back in the US and with Unichem finally helping: a better business, but after a 47% rise the price already reflects it. On the street's P/E method we see {{dcf.upside|chg}}
cover.lead: Ipca is India's 16th-largest drug maker (2.08% share), with 53% of domestic sales in pain and rheumatology (Zerodol, HCQS, Folitrax), branded exports to Africa, CIS and Asia, UK/EU and US generics, anti-malarial tenders and ~80 APIs it makes itself; it owns 52.67% of listed Unichem Laboratories. Q1FY27 revenue rose 21% to ₹2,788 cr (domestic +13%, export formulations +34%, APIs +30%), EBITDA 50% (margin 22.9%) and profit to shareholders 72%; management raised FY27 guidance to 14-16% growth and a ~23% margin. We forecast EPS of ₹58.2 / 68.0 / 78.9 for FY27-29E. Six of the seven brokers that disclose a method use **P/E** on consolidated EPS after minorities, and so do we: **29x Sep-28E EPS (₹73.5)**, i.e. Ipca's 26.3x median forward P/E since the Unichem deal (on EPS before exceptional items), lifted 10.25% for the pharma sector's re-rating, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,075; DCF ₹1,247; Unichem at market less 20% ₹2,070. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A franchise that compounds, with a cost edge
arguments.p: Pain/analgesics ₹2,152 cr on IQVIA (Jul-2026), top 10 brands 38% of sales, domestic growth ahead of the market (Q1FY27 +12.6%; chronic +17.2% vs 15.2%). Ipca makes most of its own APIs, so material cost is ~25% of standalone sales and gross margin ~71%. Cardio, derma, urology and CNS (+16-25%) are the push; anti-malarials are now ~1% of domestic sales.

arguments.h: The margin story is half done
arguments.p: Standalone margin 22.7% (FY25) → 25.2% (FY26) → 26.3% (Q1FY27); management sees ~30%. Unichem 4% → 11% in a year, 13% guided, mid-teens possible. Consolidated 20.7% → ~23% guided for FY27, 25-26% aspired in 2-3 years. We model {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}: below the aspiration because freight and solvents have risen sharply.

arguments.h: Back in the US after nine years; regulatory record now clean
arguments.p: Import alerts (2015) on Ratlam, Pithampur and Silvassa were lifted in FY24 after VAI inspections; Tarapur VAI in Feb-2026. Ipca's products drove Unichem's US +27% in Q1FY27; Europe/UK generics quadrupled. Open items on 30-Sep: five observations at Unichem's Goa plant (26-Sep) and Kolhapur (Feb).

At ₹1,927 Ipca trades at 28.3x our FY28E EPS against a 26.3x median forward P/E since the Unichem deal; it rose 47% in twelve months. Our 29x gives ₹2,130, inside the street's ₹1,935-2,190 post-Q1 range but +11% away: a HOLD on our rule. Counting the pre-deal year in the history (32x) would make it a BUY; we explain why we do not.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether the margin holds near 23% as freight and solvent costs bite and the institutional catch-up reverses; Unichem's margin vs the 13% guidance.
USFDA: the outcome of Unichem's Goa inspection (five observations, 21-26 Sep 2026) and of the Kolhapur API inspection; any new inspections at Ipca's plants.
Monthly IQVIA data: chronic growth vs the market; anti-malarial decline; pricing on non-controlled products.
Capacity: Dewas formulations (₹275 cr), Pithampur mAb plant (₹250 cr) and the Pisgah (US) plant starting trial production in FY27; Krebs merger approvals.
FY28 guidance with the Q4FY27 results; biosimilar clinical trials from FY28.

sections.title: Ipca in one page: a pain-and-rheumatology franchise in India, branded and generic exports, its own APIs, and 52.67% of Unichem

blocks.p: Ipca is an integrated drug maker: it makes most of the active ingredients (APIs) in its own medicines and sells them in more than 100 countries. FY26 revenue was ₹9,646 cr (company) in five businesses. (1) **India branded formulations** (₹3,817 cr, 40%): rank 16 in the Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) with a 2.08% share, ~7,000 medical representatives in 22 divisions, 172 brands; 53% of sales in pain and rheumatology (the Zerodol family, HCQS, Folitrax), 17% cardio-diabetic, then derma, urology, anti-bacterials, CNS. (2) **Branded exports** (₹664 cr): its own field forces in French-speaking Africa, CIS, Asia and LatAm. (3) **Generic exports** (₹1,149 cr ex-tenders): UK/EU (own label in the UK), Australia/NZ, Canada and, since the FY24 lifting of the USFDA import alerts, the US. (4) **Institutional** (₹270 cr): anti-malarial tenders for donor-funded programmes. (5) **APIs** (₹1,396 cr, 75% exported): ~80 molecules from Ratlam and other plants, sold to drug makers worldwide. On top sit the **subsidiaries** (₹2,303 cr net): mainly Unichem Laboratories (US generics, Europe, Brazil), plus Trophic Wellness (nutraceuticals), Onyx (UK research services) and Pisgah (US APIs).

sections.title: From the Bachchan-backed takeover of 1975 to a ₹49,000 cr company: the USFDA ban, the COVID boom, the bust and the Unichem bet

blocks.p: Ipca was incorporated in Mumbai in 1949 as The Indian Pharmaceutical Combine Association. Premchand Godha, a chartered accountant who handled the Bachchan family's finances, joined the board in 1975 when the family invested, became MD in 1983; in 1997 the company's four whole-time directors bought the Bachchans' 36% (the Godha and Chandurkar families are today's promoters). Under him Ipca built two things that still define it: a pain and anti-malarial franchise in India and emerging markets, and backward integration into APIs. The 2014-16 USFDA ban on its three main plants shut it out of the US for nine years; the COVID-19 boom (hydroxychloroquine) gave it a record FY21; the FY22-23 bust halved profit; and in 2023 it bought control of Unichem Laboratories, a struggling Mumbai peer with a US business and a USFDA-approved plant in Goa.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** Ipca bought Unichem for what it could not build quickly after nine years outside the US: a working US front end and an approved US plant. It paid ~₹2,930 cr for 100% of a loss-making company, close to the top of Ipca's own share-price cycle (the stock fell 15% in the week of the announcement). Three years on, the strategic logic is visible (Ipca's products drive Unichem's US growth) but the economics are still thin. Because Unichem stays listed with 47% outside holders, every rupee of synergy is shared; a merger would fix that but would cost Ipca shares.

sections.title: The industry: India's drug market grows ~10%, tilting to chronic; generics abroad are a price game where clean plants are scarce

blocks.p: India's domestic formulations market was worth ₹2,565 bn (₹2.57 lakh cr) in FY26, up 9.9% (IQVIA). Growth comes from price (4-5% a year: scheduled drugs follow a wholesale-price formula, others may rise up to 10%), new products (~2-4%) and volume (low single digits). Chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, CNS, urology) grow faster than acute (anti-infectives, pain, cough), and the market rewards companies with large, old brands that doctors trust. Abroad, Ipca competes in three different games: branded generics in emerging markets (field-force driven, currency risk), regulated generics in the UK/EU, Australia, Canada and the US (price erosion, supply reliability, regulatory compliance), and APIs (cost and reliability; Chinese competition).

bullets: **Pain is a big, slow, old-brand market.** Ipca's Zerodol family (aceclofenac combinations) and HCQS are among India's largest brands; pain grew ~11-13% for Ipca, close to the market. Its rheumatology position (HCQS, Folitrax) is hard to dislodge but also price-controlled in parts.

**Anti-malarials are fading.** Domestic anti-malarials fell 21-24% a quarter through FY26 and are now ~1-2% of Ipca's domestic sales (6% in FY20); institutional anti-malarial tenders depend on donor funding, which tightened in FY26.

**GLP-1s.** Semaglutide's Indian patent expired in Mar-2026 and many companies launched; Ipca was not in the first wave and is looking to in-license (Q3FY26 call). It matters for Ipca's small anti-diabetic franchise, not for pain.

**Input costs and freight.** The West Asia conflict lifted solvent prices 40-50%, packaging (aluminium, PVC) and freight (a US container from ~US$7,000-7,500 to $12,500-13,000; South America ~3x) from Feb-2026 (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls).
**Clean US plants are scarce.** Years of USFDA action against Indian plants make an approved, VAI-rated site a real asset; Ipca regained that status in FY24 after nine years.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Ipca's core market (India branded) grows ~10% a year with little cyclicality; its other markets are where the cycles come from. The structural change for Ipca is not the market but its own position: back in the US after nine years, and pushing into chronic therapies where it is under-represented.

sections.title: Does the market's growth reach Ipca? In India chronic and in regulated generics, yes; in anti-malarials and tenders, it runs the other way

blocks.p: Ipca has grown faster than the IPM for several quarters (Q3FY26 +10.6% vs +8.9%; Q1FY27 IQVIA +11.7% with both acute and chronic ahead), with volume growth (~5%) above the industry. Two of its own drags are fading in importance: anti-malarials (now ~1% of domestic sales) and the institutional business (₹270 cr). The regulated-markets tailwind is the newest: Europe/UK generics quadrupled in Q1FY27 and Ipca's own US products are finally selling. The headwinds are cost-side (freight, solvents) and the slow pace of Unichem's own portfolio.

sections.title: India branded formulations (40% of revenue): pain pays the bills, anti-malarials have faded, cardio and derma are the push

blocks.p: Domestic formulations doubled from ₹1,913 cr (FY20) to ₹3,817 cr (FY26), 12% a year, and grew 12.6% to ₹1,082 cr in Q1FY27. Ipca's strength is a handful of very large, old brands in pain and rheumatology: the Zerodol family (aceclofenac and combinations), HCQS (hydroxychloroquine, used in rheumatoid arthritis and lupus), Folitrax (methotrexate) and Saaz: pain/analgesics was ₹2,152 cr of IQVIA sales in the year to Jul-2026, 39% of the total, growing 11-12% a year. Its top 10 brands are ₹2,135 cr, 38% of IQVIA sales. Anti-malarials, once a signature franchise, fell from 6% of domestic sales in FY20 to 2% in FY26 and ~1% in Q1FY27. The push is into chronic therapies: cardio-diabetic (17%; CTD, CTD-T), derma, urology, CNS and ophthalmology, each growing 16-25%, after a reorganisation of the cardio division at the start of FY26. Growth in Q1FY27 split into ~5% volume (above the industry), 4.5-5% price and ~2% new products.

bullets: **Field force:** ~7,000 medical representatives; expansion "completed", with ~200 more for new divisions in FY27 (Q1FY27 call). Ipca launches few products (18-20 a year across 20-odd divisions) to keep focus on power brands.
**Pricing:** normally 5-6% a year on non-controlled products; 6-7% planned in FY27 to offset input costs; price-controlled (NLEM) products cannot move.
**Guidance:** 12-13% growth for FY27 (1-2pp from new products); management says chronic growth is now in line with the market and acute ahead of it.
**Gaps:** no first-wave GLP-1 launch; small in respiratory and gastro; anti-infectives barely growing (+1% in Q1FY27).

blocks.callout: **So what:** the India business is a steady compounder, not a growth story: market-plus growth (we model 12.5 / 11.5 / 11%) at margins we estimate in the high 20s to 30s, earned by brands built over decades. Its risk is concentration: pain is over half of it, and some of its biggest molecules are price-controlled.

sections.title: Exports (22% of revenue): branded emerging markets and UK/EU generics are growing fast; institutional anti-malarials are shrinking

blocks.p: Export formulations were ₹2,083 cr in FY26 (+9%) and ₹603 cr in Q1FY27 (+34%). They are three different businesses. **Branded (₹664 cr, +14%):** Ipca's own brands sold by its own field forces in French-speaking West Africa (the fastest, +41% in 9MFY26), CIS (₹228 cr of formulations; flat in Q3FY26 with the war), Asia and LatAm. **Generics (₹1,149 cr ex-tenders, +17%):** the UK (own label, after a loss-making FY26 for the UK subsidiary as prices collapsed), the EU (Germany subsidiary set up in FY26), Australia/NZ (₹314 cr), Canada and the US, where Ipca's approved products are sold through Unichem USA (8 marketed, 6-8 more commercialised in FY27, 46 ANDAs filed and 32 approved). In Q1FY27 Europe/UK went from ₹33 cr to ₹137 cr. **Institutional (₹270 cr, −24%):** anti-malarial tenders for donor-funded programmes, which management now expects at ₹260-300 cr a year.

It is also where prices are least secure (the UK lost money in FY26) and where a USFDA setback would hurt. We model generics +20% / +14% / +12% and institutional +5% / +3% / +3%.

sections.title: APIs (15% of revenue): the backward integration behind Ipca's 71% gross margin, and a cyclical business in its own right

blocks.p: Ipca makes ~80 APIs and intermediates, most of the molecules in its own brands (hydroxychloroquine, aceclofenac, anti-malarials, cardiovascular and anti-infective APIs), and sells the surplus to drug makers in 100+ countries (75% exported; Europe ₹362 cr, Americas ₹321 cr, Asia ₹264 cr in FY26). The integration does two things. It keeps material cost low: ~25% of standalone sales in FY26 (24% in Q3FY26, 28.7% in 9MFY25), so consolidated gross margin is ~71%. And it gives Ipca security of supply: the Krebs merger is explicitly about a fermentation API used in its largest-selling brand. External API sales are cyclical: ₹1,506 cr in FY21, ₹1,249 cr in FY24, ₹1,396 cr in FY26, then +30% to ₹424 cr in Q1FY27 as volumes and prices recovered. Ratlam is running out of capacity; a ₹182 cr intermediates plant at Wardha started in Feb-2026 and more API capacity is being built at Dewas, with continuous-process conversions.

bullets: **Regulatory depth:** 62 EDQM certificates of suitability and 50 US DMFs; Ratlam (Ipca's largest API site) has been VAI since its Jun-2023 USFDA inspection; Tarapur VAI in Feb-2026; WHO prequalification inspection of Ratlam API in Oct-2025.

**Unichem:** Unichem's own API business grew from ₹33-34 cr to ₹58 cr in Q1FY27 as it makes more of its own inputs; Ipca's APIs replacing bought-in ones in Unichem's US products need USFDA approvals (CBE-30 or prior approval), one product approved so far (Q1FY27 call).
**Pricing:** management says API cost increases are passed on fully (Q4FY26 call); prices were not renegotiated down after the rupee fell (Q1FY27 call).

blocks.callout: **So what:** APIs are both a cost moat for the formulations business and a cyclical earnings line. FY27 starts strong; we model +15% / +10% / +10%, below Q1's pace because Ratlam is near capacity until Dewas and Wardha ramp up.

sections.title: Unichem and the subsidiaries (24% of revenue): margins from 4% to 11% in a year; the US front end is now selling Ipca's products

blocks.p: Unichem (52.67% owned, listed) had revenue of ₹2,202 cr in FY26 (+4%) and ₹633 cr in Q1FY27 (+20%). Most of it is US generics made at its Goa plant and sold by Unichem Pharmaceuticals (USA), which since FY26 also sells Ipca's US products (Bayshore, Ipca's former US arm, was folded in and sold). FY26 was poor: Unichem lost high-volume US products, its own portfolio grew ~2%, its margin fell to ~8% (12.6% in FY25), it closed its Irish plant (severance; overheads of €4-5 mn a year end in FY27), and it paid the EU perindopril fine and interest. Q1FY27 turned: US +27% (Unichem's own products +9%, Ipca's much faster), Brazil +52%, ROW ₹8 cr → ₹17 cr, APIs ₹33-34 cr → ₹58 cr, margin 11%. Management guides +10% revenue and a 13% margin for FY27, rising as filings in Europe, Australia, Canada and Chile convert (~1.5 years after filing). The other subsidiaries: Trophic Wellness (58.88%; nutraceuticals, ~₹125 cr of sales and ~₹40 cr of profit), Pisgah Laboratories (US APIs; a US$22 mn liquid-injectables plant due for trial production in FY27), Onyx Scientific (UK research services; weak demand) and Ipca's UK and German generics arms (the UK lost £2-3 mn in FY26).

sections.title: The USFDA record: nine years under import alert (2015-2023), all plants clean on 30-Sep-2026, two Unichem inspections open

blocks.p: Ipca's US story is a regulatory one. In 2014 USFDA inspectors found data-integrity failures at the Ratlam API plant; Ipca stopped shipping, and import alerts followed on Ratlam (Jan-2015) and on its two main formulation plants, Pithampur (SEZ Indore) and Piparia (Silvassa) (Mar-2015), then a warning letter (Feb-2016). For eight years Ipca sold almost nothing in the US. In FY24 all three plants were re-inspected, classified Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI: objectionable conditions found, but no regulatory action) and taken off import alert. Since then: Tarapur API (VAI, Feb-2026), and WHO prequalification inspections of Pithampur and Ratlam in 2025. No Ipca or Unichem plant was under a USFDA import alert or warning letter on 30-Sep-2026. Two Unichem inspections were open (Kolhapur API: no EIR reported; Goa formulations: 5 observations on 26-Sep-2026).

blocks.p: Ipca's moat is the combination of doctor loyalty to a few large pain and rheumatology brands and the cost advantage of making their APIs in-house. It protects margins in India and gives it staying power in API-driven export markets. It does not give pricing power (many molecules are price-controlled; generics abroad are commodities) or a growth engine of its own; that is what the biosimilar and regulated-generics investments are meant to build.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** narrow moat. Ipca deserves a multiple near the Indian branded-pharma pack for its domestic franchise and balance sheet, but not a premium: its ROE (15% in FY26, ~17% in our forecasts) is respectable, not exceptional, and half its business is cyclical.

sections.title: Revenue ×2.6 since FY19, but margins went round a full cycle: 29% in the COVID year, 15% in FY23, 23% again in Q1FY27

blocks.p: Ipca's revenue grew from ₹3,746 cr in FY19 to ₹9,599 cr in FY26 (14% a year), in three phases. **FY19-21:** a boom, as anti-malarial and hydroxychloroquine demand peaked with COVID-19 and API prices rose; EBITDA margin reached 28.8% and EPS ₹44.9 in FY21. **FY22-23:** the bust: hydroxychloroquine normalised, institutional anti-malarial tenders shrank, API prices fell while solvent and raw-material costs rose; margin fell to 15.0% and EPS to ₹18.6 in FY23 (−47%). **FY24-26:** the rebuild: Unichem (consolidated from Sep-2023) added ~₹1,500-2,300 cr of revenue at low margins, while Ipca's own business recovered: standalone margin rose from 22.7% in FY25 to 25.2% in FY26 and 26.3% in Q1FY27 (excluding forex gains), as material cost fell from ~28.7% to ~25% of standalone sales on mix. Consolidated margin climbed from 17.3% (FY24) to 20.7% (FY26) and 22.9% in Q1FY27 (company basis). EPS to shareholders was ₹44.98 in FY26 (₹44.6 before exceptional items and the one-off Bayshore gain), back to the FY21 peak five years later.

bullets: **A clean beat, with three helpers:** EBITDA was ~20-27% above broker estimates (Emkay, PL). The stock rose 12% to a record ₹1,945 on 17-Aug-2026.

**IQVIA:** Ipca +11.7% on IQVIA (chronic 17.2% vs market 15.2%; acute 8.9% vs 4.5%); rank 16, market share 2.08%; anti-malarials −24%, now ~1% of the domestic business; pain +13%, cardio-diabetic +17%, CNS +19%, derma +17%, urology +25%, ophthalmology +17%; ~5% volume, 4.5-5% price, ~2% new products.

sections.title: Capital allocation: self-funded capex and one big deal (Unichem, ₹1,543 cr); two small bets on Krebs and Lyka went badly

blocks.p: Ipca funds itself. Over FY22-26 it generated ₹5,070 cr of operating cash flow and spent ₹2,816 cr on capex (6-9% of revenue: APIs, new formulation plants, biotech), ₹406 cr on dividends (₹4 a share a year, ₹6 for FY26) and ₹1,543 cr on Unichem. Borrowings rose to ₹1,481 cr by Mar-23 (cash then ₹1,853 cr) and the cash went on Unichem in FY24; debt was back to ₹704 cr (plus leases) by Mar-26, of which ₹469 cr sits in Unichem. Return on capital followed the cycle: ROCE 31% in FY21, 11% in FY23, 17% in FY26 (Screener).

blocks.callout: **The Unichem arithmetic.** Ipca paid ₹1,543 cr for 52.67%, valuing the whole company at ~₹2,930 cr, for a business that lost money at the EBITDA level in FY23. Three years on, Unichem's market value is ₹3,840 cr and its margin has gone from negative to 11%. It has not yet earned its cost of capital: Ipca's share of Unichem's profit was roughly ₹68 cr in our FY27E, a ~4.4% return on the price.

sections.title: Earnings quality: decent cash conversion, but read the exceptional items, the forex line and the minorities carefully

bullets: **Exceptional items every year:** FY24 −₹107.75 cr (Unichem's EU fine provision ₹125.62 cr, deal costs ₹39.04 cr, Krebs impairment ₹11.10 cr, less a ₹64.78 cr gain on Optimus shares), FY25 −₹205.05 cr (Krebs impairment ₹118.90 cr, Unichem land impairment ₹86.15 cr), FY26 −₹86.43 cr (EU interest ₹58.26 cr, labour codes ₹45.82 cr, land gain ₹17.65 cr). Screener books them in other income. Most relate to Unichem and Krebs, i.e. to past capital-allocation decisions.

**One-off gains in other income:** FY26 other income of ₹174 cr included ₹60.04 cr on deconsolidating Bayshore and ₹5.31 cr on selling a business; we remove the Bayshore gain from the FY26 base (EPS ₹44.6 vs the company's ₹46.94 before exceptional items).
**Forex:** gains are booked inside other expenses (₹31.7 cr in Q1FY27), so Screener's EBITDA (24.0%) is above the company's (22.88%). We forecast neither forex gains nor losses.

**Minorities:** 47.33% of Unichem and 41.12% of Trophic Wellness; ₹42.7 cr in FY26, ~₹21 cr in Q1FY27, rising with Unichem's recovery (our ₹80 / 103 / 129 cr). The engine has no minority line, so our tax line carries them.

**Cash conversion:** operating cash flow was 71-97% of EBITDA in FY22-25 and 57% in FY26 (working capital −₹294 cr, taxes ₹414 cr; Screener). Working capital is structurally heavy (~144 days); Ipca says its own has been flat for two years, Unichem carries US stock in transit.
**Capitalisation:** capex ran at 7-9% of revenue in FY22-26 while D&A was 4-5%; R&D is expensed (₹246 cr, 3.4% of standalone turnover in FY26).

**Auditor and contingencies:** N V C & Associates LLP; contingent liabilities ₹249 cr; no emphasis of matter found in the consolidated audit report; the Unichem auditor flagged a key audit matter on its own accounts.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Revenue and cost recognition look conservative and the balance sheet is clean. But reported EPS has been distorted by exceptional items in each of the last three years, FY26 carries a one-off gain inside other income, and the forex line moves Screener's margin. We value Ipca on EPS before exceptional items and one-offs, and show reported EPS alongside.

sections.title: Balance sheet: net cash again, but working capital is heavy (~144 days) and Unichem keeps its own debt

blocks.p: At Mar-26 Ipca had ₹1,225 cr of cash, bank deposits and liquid funds (of which Unichem ₹295 cr) against ₹704 cr of borrowings (Unichem ₹469 cr, mostly working-capital lines; Ipca ₹235 cr of cheap term loans) and ₹105 cr of leases: net cash of ₹416 cr including leases (₹600 cr on Screener's basis, which also counts the ₹184 cr Krebs and Lyka stakes). Ipca repaid ~US$50 mn of dollar loans before the rupee fell and its term loans were ~₹193 cr at Jun-26, falling to ~₹70 cr by Mar-27. On our numbers net cash rises to ₹854 / 1,678 / 2,783 cr at Mar-27/28/29. The weak spot is working capital: inventory ₹2,731 cr and receivables ₹2,014 cr against payables of ₹940 cr; net working capital is ~39% of revenue (~144 days, PL), because Ipca carries large API, raw-material and export inventories, and Unichem's US business adds stock in transit.

sections.title: Ownership: the Godha and Chandurkar families own 44.7%; domestic mutual funds own almost a third

blocks.p: Two families control Ipca: the Godhas (Executive Chairman Premchand Godha and his sons Pranay, MD & CEO, and Prashant, Executive Director; mainly through Kaygee Investments, 25.49%, and Kaygee Laboratories, 6.61%) and the Chandurkars (Chandurkar Investments 5.50%, Usha Chandurkar 1.70%, Sameer Chandurkar 0.79%). Promoters own 44.72% (Jun-2026), with no pledge. Domestic institutions own 37.04% (mutual funds 31.2% at Mar-26: HDFC Mutual Fund 9.60%, Kotak 6.28%, DSP 5.52%), foreign investors 10.72% and the public 7.19% (82,060 shareholders).

sections.title: Management & governance: an experienced family-plus-professional team; the succession has happened; pay and related-party bets are the weak spots

blocks.p: Premchand Godha has led Ipca since the 1980s; he handed the MD & CEO role to his son Pranay Godha (born 1972) on 1-Apr-2023 and stayed on as Executive Chairman. Day-to-day finance and investor communication sit with A.K. Jain (born 1955), Managing Director and CFO, a non-promoter professional who runs the earnings calls. Prashant Godha (born 1974) is Executive Director, re-appointed for five years from Aug-2026. Succession is therefore in place at the top, with A.K. Jain's age (71) the key-person question for the finance role. The board has eight members: four executives and four independents.

blocks.p: **Why we are a HOLD when the street says Buy.** Our EPS is at the top of the range (FY28E ₹68.0 vs ₹62.7-68.3); the difference is the multiple. The P/E houses apply 25-30x to forward EPS (MOSL and PL 30x), close to our 29x, so our target (₹2,130) sits inside the street's range (₹1,935-2,190). What we do not share is the urgency: at ₹1,927 the stock already trades at 28.3x our FY28E EPS, above Ipca's 26.3x median one-year-forward P/E since the Unichem deal, after rising 47% in twelve months. The upside left (+11%) is below the 15% our rule requires for a BUY.

sections.title: Valuation: 29x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, +11% from ₹1,927: HOLD

blocks.p: Of the notes standing on 30-Sep-2026 that disclose a method, six value Ipca on **P/E** (Motilal Oswal 30x 12-month-forward EPS, Prabhudas Lilladher 30x FY28E, Choice 25x FY28E, HDFC Securities 28x Q3FY28E, Sharekhan 45x FY28E, and Emkay on Sep-28E EPS with Unichem at a separate multiple) and one on **EV/EBITDA** (ICICI Direct 18x FY28E). We follow the majority: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, the EPS a buyer will look at one year from now. Like the street we value **consolidated EPS after minorities**, so Unichem enters through Ipca's 52.67% share of its profit and is not counted again as a listed stake; a sum-of-the-parts with the stake at market less 20% is shown as a sensitivity. EV/EBITDA (ICICI Direct's method) and a DCF are cross-checks.

The house rule (PLAYBOOK §4) starts from the stock's own one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, leaving out trough years. Two things make Ipca's history need care. **(1) Exceptional items** were large in FY24-26 (−₹108 / −205 / −86 cr) and FY26 also carried a ₹60 cr one-off gain on deconsolidating Bayshore; as in our Sun Pharma, Cipla and Torrent reports, the base uses **EPS before exceptional items and one-offs** (forecasts carry none) and the reported-EPS median is a sensitivity. **(2) Unichem.** From FY24 every EPS figure includes Unichem (and the deal's financing), while share prices before the deal (24-Apr-2023) priced Ipca without it. To keep history and forecasts on one basis, the base window starts on **2023-04-25**, the first trading day after the deal: every point then divides a price that includes Unichem by EPS that includes Unichem. We use every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (180 points), multiply the median by the pharma sector factor (+10.25%, the median of the other eight peers, PLAYBOOK §7c A20) and round to the nearest half-turn. No own de-rating, growth or returns adjustment enters the base.

blocks.p: Unichem is listed and Ipca owns 52.67%. There are two clean ways to value it, and they must not be mixed. **The street's way (our base):** value Ipca's consolidated EPS after minorities, so Ipca's share of Unichem's profit (~₹105 cr in Sep-28E, ₹4.2 of EPS) is valued at 29x, implicitly ₹3,055 cr for the stake. **The sum of the parts:** value Ipca without Unichem (EPS ₹69.3) at 29x and add the stake at its 30-Sep-2026 market value less 20% (PLAYBOOK §7c holding discount): ₹2,023 cr × 0.8 = ₹1,618 cr (₹64 a share). That gives ₹2,070, −3% vs our target. The two are close because Unichem is a small part of Ipca's EPS (₹4.2 of ₹73.5). The consolidated method implicitly values the stake at ₹3,055 cr, above its ₹2,023 cr market value (Unichem trades at ~31.7x its own trailing earnings, which include a land-sale gain), so the sum of the parts comes out ₹57 a share lower. We keep the street's consolidated method; the gap would close if Unichem's margin reaches the mid-teens we assume.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than three years ago at a price that already says so; HOLD

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading pain and rheumatology franchise with market-plus growth; an integrated API base that keeps gross margin ~71%; branded emerging-market and regulated-generics businesses growing double digit; clean USFDA status regained after nine years; a net-cash balance sheet; and 52.67% of a recovering Unichem. **What you are not buying:** pricing power, a proprietary pipeline (biosimilars are FY29-30 at the earliest) or a business free of cycles: anti-malarials, tenders, APIs and currency can swing a year by 20-40%.

**What you are paying:** ₹1,927 is 37.3x trailing EPS, 33.1x our FY27E and 28.3x our FY28E EPS, against a 26.3x median one-year-forward P/E since the Unichem deal (on EPS before exceptional items). Pharma peers trade 10.25% above their five-year medians; Ipca's trailing P/E is 8% below its own. On the street's method (P/E) and our derived 29x, the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a HOLD. EV/EBITDA (₹2,075) agrees; the DCF (₹1,247 at 11.6%) says the price leans on the multiple, as it does for most of the sector.
